svg.title: Small Enough to Understand
svg.desc: Sketch in perspective: a bicycle stands side-on between two mannequins, its front frame triangle hatched. Every part is drawn in the open: two wheels, the chain and gear, the saddle, and the handlebars. In front, one figure points at the chain and gear; behind the bicycle, the other reaches a wrench to the front wheel's hub. The bicycle is the system from the pattern's context, the hardware and software a group chooses. Its few, visible parts are the solution, a system small enough to understand, so the frame is the focus. The figure pointing knows how it works; the figure with the wrench is a second member learning to look after it, the person who could learn to run it in a weekend. The metaphor: a system as a bicycle rather than a sealed engine. Anyone can see how it works and a friend can fix it, at the cost the pattern names: it won't go as fast or as far as a car.
